convention: A Chinese month starts on the UTC+8 civil date of the astronomical new moon. JDE is Terrestrial Time; UTC = JDE - Delta T; the civil date is the UTC+08:00 date of that instant.

conflicts.classification: HKO lists 1914-11-17 while the documented UTC+8 rule places the new moon 1m43s after local midnight on 1914-11-18, so this dataset keeps 1914-11-18. Why HKO's 1914 row uses the previous UT date is unresolved; the available sources do not establish an intentional historical UT-date convention.
